screens.instruction: Select the correct kanji: どりょく (effort)
screens.prompt: [ ]力 (力 pre-filled)
screens.feedback: 努力 | effort | 努 is a combination of 女 (woman), 又 (again), and 力 (power).
screens.image: photo of two women doing sit-up exercises

screens.instruction: Select the correct kanji: しあい (match; race)
screens.feedback: 試合 | match; race | 試 is a combination of 言 (to say) and 式 (ceremony).
screens.image: photo of a baseball batter at a game

screens.instruction: Select the correct kanji: しけん (exam)
screens.feedback: 試験 | exam | There is a theory that the kanji 験 (test) comes from the practice of gathering horses (馬) together and grading them.
screens.image: photo of a student writing at a desk

screens.prompt: 医者になる[ ][ ]をうけたいので、毎日[ ][ ]しています。

screens.feedback: 医者になる試験をうけたいので、毎日努力しています。 | I've been making an effort every day because I want to take an exam to become a doctor. | The readings of the kanji are: 試験 / しけん and 努力 / どりょく.
screens.image: photo of a woman in scrubs with a stethoscope at a laptop

screens.type: match pairs (two parts of a sentence)
screens.instruction: Match the two parts of the sentences.
screens.correct: 私は努力を=続けます。; 雨の日が=続きます。
screens.feedback: Let's focus on the おくりがな and particles: (を) つづ-ける (to continue), (が) つづ-く (something continues)

screens.prompt: 通う - [ ]う、通る - [ ]る
screens.feedback: 通う - かよう、通る - とおる | to commute; to pass | Depending on the word, the kanji 通 can be read as かよ-う, とお-る or つう.

explanations: 学生が学校に通うこと
病気の人が病院に通うこと

screens.feedback: 通う / かよう means "to travel between our home and another place on a regular basis": 通学 /つうがく, 通院 / つういん.

screens.prompt: We see 通 a lot on maps and street signs because it means "street". | 竹下通り / たけしたどおり in Harajuku is a popular gathering spot for young people as it has many trendy shops, fashion boutiques and fast food outlets. | 竹下通り / たけしたどおり (Takeshita street)

screens.image: photo of a person in a beret on a busy colourful shopping street

screens.instruction: Why does the woman want to continue the cooking class?
screens.feedback: すばらしい体験 | wonderful experience | 体験 / たいけん is used when talking about a one-off or short trial experience.

This exam is for getting into 高校, or 大学 if students want to continue their education. | It is less common, but some pupils even take 入試 to get into private 小学校 and 中学校. | 入試 / にゅうし、入学試験 / にゅうがくしけん (school entrance exam)

screens.feedback: 一月から三月は入試のきせつです。 | January to March is the season for entrance exams. | The school year starts in April in Japan, so a lot of 入試 take place between January and March.
screens.image: photo of students sitting an exam in a classroom

screens.type: select the correct kanji (drag one option into the slot)

screens.feedback: 一位 | first place | 位 is a combination of 亻(person) and 立 (stand) because winners stand on a podium!

screens.type: select the correct kanji (drag one option into the slot)
screens.instruction: Select the correct kanji: やきゅう (baseball)
screens.feedback: 野球 | baseball | 求 and 球 are read as きゅう. This is because they both include 求. But kanji don't always follow this pattern!
screens.image: photo of a baseball batter at a game

screens.prompt: [ ][ ]の試合で二[ ]でした。[ ][ ]できませんでした。

screens.instruction: What does the woman intend to do?

screens.correct: 初めは日本のチームが優位だったけど、負けてしまいました。
screens.feedback: 初めは日本のチームが優位だったけど、負けてしまいました。 | The Japanese team had an advantage at the beginning, but regrettably, they lost. | 優 means "superiority" and 位 means "rank; position".
screens.image: photo of wheelchair racers on a track

screens.instruction: What is the man continuing to put effort into?
screens.feedback: 学位 | degree | The man said 学位 (がくい)をとりたい. 学 means "learning", 位 means "rank; position".
screens.image: photo of three students looking at a laptop

screens.feedback: 電球 | light bulb | 電 means "electricity" and 球 means "ball".
screens.image: photo of a hand screwing in a light bulb

lessons.lessonLabel: Kanji: 館 段 庭 室 性

screens.instruction: Select the correct word with kanji: かん (building)
screens.feedback: 館 | building | The radical of 館 is ⻟. We eat meals in 旅館 and popcorn in 映画館!

screens.instruction: Select the correct word with kanji: かいだん (stairs)
screens.prompt: 階[ ] (階 pre-filled)
screens.feedback: 階段 | stairs | The radical of 段 is ⽎ meaning "hitting; beating".

screens.prompt: The "black belt" is a symbol of an expert in judo, but did you know that there are even higher levels? | Becoming a black belt means that someone is in 初段 / しょだん (the 1st "dan" grade). Then they go up to 二段 / にだん, 三段 / さんだん etc. After 五段 / ごだん, they can wear a red-and-white belt. After 九段 / きゅうだん, the colour of their belt becomes solid red. | 私は柔道三段です。柔道教室で子供たちに教えています。(I am a 3rd dan in judo. I teach children in judo class.)

lessons.lessonLabel: Kanji: 遊 疲 吸 別 直

screens.instruction: Select the correct kanji: あそ-ぶ (to play)
screens.feedback: 遊ぶ | to play | If we look at the different parts of 遊, there's a child (子) moving (⻌) in different directions (方).

screens.instruction: Select the correct kanji: つか-れる (to be tired)
screens.feedback: 疲れる | to be tired | The radical of 疲 is ⽧, meaning "illness". Other kanji with the same radical are 病 (びょう) and 痛 (いた-い).

screens.prompt: 私は[ ]れたので、子供達だけで[ ]ばせました。
screens.feedback: 私は疲れたので、子供達だけで遊ばせました。 | I got tired, so I let my children play on their own. | The readings of the kanji are: 疲れた / つかれた and 遊ばせました / あそばせました.

screens.instruction: Select the correct kanji: す-う (to breathe in)
screens.feedback: 吸う | to breathe in | The radical of 吸 is ⼝ (mouth), as it is something we do with our mouths!

screens.instruction: Select the correct kanji: わか-れる (to separate; to break up)
screens.feedback: 別れる | to separate; to break up | The radical of 別 is 刀 (sword), which separates one thing from another.

screens.prompt: 彼女と[ ]れてから、たばこを[ ]うのをやめました。
screens.feedback: 彼女と別れてから、たばこを吸うのをやめました。 | After breaking up with my girlfriend, I stopped smoking cigarettes. | The readings of the kanji are: 別れて / わかれて and 吸う / すう.
screens.image: photo of a man with a hand raised (media panel with audio bar)

screens.instruction: Select the correct kanji: なおす (to fix)
screens.feedback: 直す | to fix | When we're fixing (直) something, it would be good to have ten (十) eyes (目) and a tool (乚).
screens.image: photo of two men at a car bonnet

screens.prompt: 直す means "to fix" an error or "repair" something broken. It can also mean "to tidy or neaten" something, especially hair, clothes, or makeup. Examples: こわれた車を直す (to fix a broken car); ネクタイを直す (to straighten my tie); 化粧 / けしょうを直す (to touch up my makeup).
面接の前に、ネクタイを[ ]して、大きく[ ]を[ ]いました。
screens.feedback: 面接の前に、ネクタイを直して、大きく息を吸いました。 | Before the interview, I straightened my tie and took a deep breath. | The readings of the kanji are: 直して / なおして, 息 / いき, and 吸いました / すいました.
screens.image: photo of a man in a suit adjusting his tie
screens.notes: 息 is an extra tile here (not a kanji of this lesson).

screens.prompt: When 直す / なおす is used after the ます stem of another verb, it means "to do something again". 書き直す (to rewrite); 読み直す (to reread); 考え直す (to reconsider).
読み[ ]める、読み[ ]わる、読み[ ]す
screens.feedback: 読み始める、読み終わる、読み直す | to start reading, to finish reading, to reread | Like 〜始める and 〜終わる, 直す / なおす can be used with the ます stem to say "to do something again".

screens.prompt: 先生は私に作文を書き直させました。 / The teacher made me start writing an essay.
screens.feedback: 書き直す means "to rewrite". 直す is used after the ます stem of another verb to say "to do something again".
screens.image: photo of a teacher with students
screens.notes: The English statement says 'start writing'; the Japanese means rewrite.
